newsitem.title: INDIA: India market regulator approves stock lending scheme.
newsitem.headline: India market regulator approves stock lending scheme.

text.p: Market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Thursday its board has approved a stock lending scheme.
Under the scheme lenders will deposit securities with an approved intermediary who must have a minimum net worth of 500 million rupees for a specified period, SEBI said in a statement.
The lender of shares will receive interest for the service and will continue to enjoy dividends and other rights on the shares, the market watchdog said.
In order to monitor trades more tightly, brokers will have to declare their net long position in each stock, SEBI said. Stock exchanges already require brokers to disclose their net short position.
The announcement was made at a news conference following a SEBI meeting on Thursday.
